title: CWG 2026 Glasgow LIVE Updates, Day 5: Bindyarani in action after Gyaneshwari wins weightlifting silver; Sreeshankar, Tejas, Lokesh qualify for athletics finals
summary: Day five of the 2026 Commonwealth Games in Glasgow saw a busy schedule for India: Bindyarani Devi won bronze in women’s 58kg weightlifting, Gyaneshwari Yadav claimed silver in the 53kg class, and Sharmila Dhankar struck gold in the women's shot put F57. Murali Sreeshankar, Tejas Shirse and Lokesh Sathyanathan progressed to athletics finals. There were strong showings across weightlifting, high jump, swimming and boxing, alongside some injury concerns and selection controversies.
content:
Welcome to Sportstar’s live coverage of Day 5 of the 23rd Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

Schedule highlights included multiple athletics events (men’s long jump qualification, 100m heats, 110m hurdles), para athletics shot put F57 final, several weightlifting finals, swimming heats and finals, and an active boxing card.

Weightlifting: The women’s 58kg and men’s 79kg competitions provided drama. India’s Bindyarani Devi took bronze in the women’s 58kg after a strong snatch phase and an intense clean-and-jerk segment. Bindyarani recorded 85kg in the snatch section and matched other competitors with efforts in the clean-and-jerk, but a final 116kg attempt was unsuccessful. Rafiatu Lawal of Nigeria dominated her category, lifting a Games and Commonwealth record total to take gold. Canada’s Ann Sophie Taschereau claimed silver in several weight classes mentioned across the session.

Gyaneshwari Yadav produced a superb performance in the women’s 53kg weightlifting, matching and then chasing Games records in a thrilling duel with Nigeria’s Onome Omolola Didih. Gyaneshwari lifted impressive weights (clean and jerk attempts up to 111kg) and finished with a 199kg total to secure silver, while Didih took gold with 206kg. The competition featured multiple lead changes and several records being set and then bettered.

Shot put F57: Sharmila Dhankar delivered a landmark moment for India, winning gold in the women’s shot put F57 with a best throw of 9.81m. Her victory ended India’s 20-year wait for a Para Athletics medal at the Commonwealth Games, making her the country’s first-ever CWG gold medallist in Para Athletics and the first Indian woman to win a Para Athletics medal at the Games. Shilpa K. Shyla moved into bronze position after a judge review in another event.

High jump: The men’s high jump final featured strong Indian representation. Sarvesh Kushare produced a steady series of clearances and secured the silver medal after clearing heights including a crucial 2.25m on his final attempt. Jamaica’s Romaine Beckford and others battled up the leaderboard, with countback and failed attempts deciding final positions. Aadarsh Ram moved into the top standings early with a 2.10m clearance but finished outside the medals after later failures. Tejaswin Shankar, who had been listed inconsistently on the official startlist, was ruled DNS for the final and later cited a knee issue that prevented him from competing further.

Athletics qualifying: Murali Sreeshankar automatically qualified for the long jump final with an opening legal jump of 8.01m. Lokesh Sathyanathan also secured a spot in the final from Group B with a decisive opening leap, and Tejas Shirse progressed from the 110m hurdles heats and later reached the final despite a concerning performance in the final where he finished eighth and appeared injured.

Swimming and para-swimming: Sajan Prakash qualified for the men’s 200m butterfly final with a strong heat, and Swatik Patil advanced to the men’s 100m breaststroke SB9 final. Aryan Nehra finished seventh in the 800m freestyle fastest heat, while other Indian swimmers posted competitive times but missed podium spots.

Boxing: Several Indian boxers advanced through round of 16 bouts. Sakshi Chaudhary won convincingly against Botswana’s Lethabo Modukanele by unanimous decision and progressed to the quarterfinals. Sachin (Vijender Singh’s nephew) claimed victory over England’s William Hewitt and moved into the next round. Sumit Kundu’s contest against Northern Ireland’s Jon McConnell ended in a split-decision defeat after a tightly scored bout.

Other notes and incidents: The Commonwealth Games official results website briefly listed Tejaswin Shankar as DNS, causing confusion when broadcast coverage showed him present. The day also featured tactical decisions in boxing (point deductions and warnings), jury reviews in weightlifting that overturned or upheld attempts, and athletes pulling out due to cramps or injury. India’s women’s wheelchair 3x3 basketball team finished their group stage with a loss to Nigeria, ending their campaign.

Overall, Day 5 combined medal success for India in para athletics and weightlifting with several athletes securing finals in athletics and swimming. Medical updates on a few injured competitors and ongoing appeals or jury decisions will shape the coming days as India chases more medals in Glasgow.

Published on Jul 27, 2026

Source: Live coverage and event reports from Scotstoun Stadium and weightlifting venues, Glasgow.

Welcome toSportstar’s live coverage of day five of the 23rd edition of the Commonwealth Games taking place in Glasgow.

Let’s quickly take a look at how power-packed today’s schedule is:

2:40 PM - Gurindervir Singh, men’s 100m Round 1-Heat 4

3:00 PM - Murali Sreeshankar, men’s long jump qualification, Group A

3:55 PM - Tejas Shirse, men’s 110m hurdles Round 1

4:20 PM - Lokesh Sathyanathan, men’s long jump qualification, Group B

11:35 PM - Sharmila Dhankar and Shilpa K. Shyla, women’s shot put F57 final

11:40 PM - Sarvesh Kushare, Aadarsh Ram, and Tejaswin Shankar, men’s high jump final

1:57 AM - Rakeshbhai Bhatt and Shreyansh Trivedi, men’s 100m T38 final (medal event)

2:15 AM - Tejas Shirse, men’s 110m hurdles final, subject to qualification (medal event)

3:00 PM - ​Sajan Prakash,​men’s 200m butterfly - Heat 2

4:26 PM - Swatik Patil, men’s 100m breaststroke SB9 - Heat 2

12:02 AM (July 28) - Swatik Patil, men’s 100m breaststroke SB9 final, subject to qualification (medal event)

1:07 AM (July 28) - Aryan Nehra, men’s 800m freestyle fastest heat/final (medal event)

1:44 AM (July 28) - Sajan Prakash, men’s 200m butterfly final, subject to qualification (medal event)

4:45 PM - ​Sachin Siwach​vs William Hewitt (England), men’s 60kg Round of 16

6:00 PM - Ankush, men’s 80kg Round of 16

10:30 PM - Sakshi Choudhary vs Lethabo Modukanele (Botswana), women’s 51kg Round of 16

1:00 AM (Tuesday) - Sumit Kundu vs Jon McConnell (Northern Ireland), men’s 70kg Round of 16

6:15 PM - ​Protistha Samanta,​women’s vault final (medal event)

5:45 PM - Gyaneshwari Yadav, women’s 53kg final (medal event)

8:00 PM - Bindyarani Devi, women’s 58kg final (medal event)

12:45 AM (July 28) - Ajaya Babu, men’s 79kg final (medal event)

10:05 PM - Putul Sonowal vs Anwar Hamada (Kenya), men’s singles Section D sectional play

12:00 AM (Tuesday) - India vs Nigeria, women’s wheelchair Pool B match

It’s track and field day at the Commonwealth Games.

Athletics is arguably the grandest event on the Glasgow roster where a couple of Indian stars, including former World and Olympic champion Neeraj Chopra, will be expected to come home with medals.

Before we get there, here’s a small introduction. My name isSantadeep Dey, and I will be taking you through the live action. Our correspondent,K. Keerthivasan, is at the venue to provide us with timely updates.

At the moment, the officials have deemed that the only valid throw of Nigeria’s Eucharia Iyiazi, which won her the bronze, is also a foul.

India’s Shilpa K. Shyla moves into the bronze medal position.

There may be a protest from the Nigerian camp.

A disappointing race for Tejas Shirse who seems to have some sort of an injury as he finishes eighth in the men’s 110m hurdles final, clocking 15.39s.

Sharmila has ended India’s 20-year wait for a Para Athletics medal at the Commonwealth Games. She also becomes India’s first-ever CWG Gold medallist in Para Athletics and the first Indian woman to win a Para Athletics medal at the Games.

Both Beckford and Kushare fail to clear 2.28m.

On countback, the Jamaican, who had a first-time clearance at 2.25m while Kushare cleared the same height on his third attempt, takes the gold.

It is silver medal for Sarvesh Kushare!

After her opening effort of 8.19m, Nigeria’s Eucharia Iyiazi commits five fouls in a row and finishes third!

Ghana’s Zinabu Issah (8.65m) wins silver andIndia’s Sharmila (9.81m) grabs the gold!

The English jumper fails twice at 2.28m and that’s it for him. He finishes third and will get the bronze.

Kimani Jack of England, who decided to skip 2.25m after one failed attempt, does not manage to clear 2.28m either. If he fails again, he is out of the competition.

Beckford also fails on his first try at 2.28m.

If Kushare clears this now, he will back in the gold medal position. Can he do it? Sadly, he can’t!

On his final attempt at 2.25m, Sarvesh Kushare finally manages to clear the bar and a medal is confirmed for the Indian.

Jamaica’s Raymond Richards finishes fourth after he fails to clear the bar thrice.

No medals for India as Rakeshbhai Bhatt and Shreyansh Trivedi finish fifth and sixth, respectively.

Jamaica’s Romaine Beckford clears 2.25m height on his first attempt and takes the lead as the other three jumps fail.

In fact, Kushare and Raymond Richards have failed twice at the same height while Jack has decided after one failed attempt that he will next have a go when the bar is raised further.

India’s Sharmila, the penultimate competitor in the field, leads the chart with a best effort of 9.81m. Her compatriot Shilpa is currently third with 7.26 while Ghana’s Zinabu Issah is currently in the silver medal position with 8.65m throw.

Only Nigeria’s Eucharia Iyiazi is left to compete.

Three failed clearances at 2.20m means India’s Aadarsh Ram is out of the competition as he finishes fifth.

Sarvesh Kushare, England’s Kimani Jack, and Jamaican duo of Romaine Beckford and Raymond Richards are the ones who will continue to compete.

India’s Sajan Prakash finishes last in the men’s 200m butterfly final with a timing of 1:58.05s.

Australia’s Yual Reath and Donald Thomas of The Bahamas fail to clear 2.15m.

Five jumpers, including India’s Aadarsh Ram and Sarvesh Kushare, are left in the competition.

India’s Sumit Kundu suffered a 1-4 defeat to Northern Ireland’s Jon McConnell in the men’s 70kg round of 16 at the Commonwealth Games 2026 on Monday, despite four of the five judges recording level totals after three rounds.

What a comeback! Ajaya Babu sets a new Commonwealth Games snatch record with a massive 149kg lift. The Indian leads after the snatch section heading into the clean and jerk.

At 2.10m, Isle of Man’s Regan Corrin, Fiji’s Rusiate Matai and Singapore’s Kampton Kam bow out.

After successfully lifting 145, Ajaya’s second attempt of 149kg failed. He lifted the weight, which pushed him backwards, and he lost balance. He has another snatch attempt left.

With three more competitors (including a compatriot) to go, India’s Shilpa K. Shyla is in the gold medal position courtesy her throw of 7.26m which came in her third attempt.

India’s Sumit Kundu has lost his round of 16 bout to Northern Ireland’s Jon McConnell in a heart-breaking manner.

Both boxer’s had equal scores according to four out of five judges while according to the fifth judge, Sumit was the winner.

However, McConnell, who received a point penalty in the first round, won the next two rounds.

The judges rule that McConnell is the winner via a split decision.

Ajaya holds his ground and successfully lifts 145kg in his first attempt in the snatch category. He is going for 149kg in his next attempt.

Aryan Nehra finishes 7th in men’s 800m freestyle with a timing of 8:07.26s. Australia’s Sam Short (7:39.81s) bags the gold, Benjamin Goedemans (7:46.49s) takes the silver while the bronze goes to Matthew Galea (7:47.10s). An all-Australian podium!

India’s Aadarsh Ram moves to the top of the standings as he clears 2.10m with his first leap of the competition in the men’s high jump final.

Sarvesh Kushare, the other Indian left in the competition, also clears the bar set at 2.10m with his first attempt.

Sri Lanka’s Tharindu Dasun Samaraweera finishes with “No Mark” against his name as he fails to clear 2.05m.

Kenya’s Kemboi Asbel Kiprop, Anguilla’s J’Quan Samuels and Dezardin Prosper from Mauritius are also out after three failed attempts at the same height.

In its third and final group-stage game, the Indian women’s team has lost 6-7 to Nigeria to finish at the bottom of Pool B.

It means India’s campaign is over as it cannot progress to the knockouts.

Tejaswin Shankar seems to have a knee issue. He failed to clear the bar set at 2.05m in what was his jump of the competition before informing the officials that he cannot continue.

The high jump bronze medallist from Birmingham 2022 is due to compete in decathlon this time and the Indian track and field fans will hope that he gets well soon.

After more than an hour, we finally have a jump from one of the three Indians. Sarvesh Kushare, the National Record-holder, starts with an easy clearance at 2.05m.

As the high jump final continues under overcast skies, medal hopefuls battle it out outdoors. Meanwhile, indoors, Ajaya Babu is ready for action in the men’s 79kg weightlifting event and will open his snatch campaign with a 145kg attempt. We will keep you updated on his progress.

The majority of the field is still very much in the competition while some are yet to even begin.

Australia’s Yual Reath is finally ready for his first jump of the contest and he clears the bar on his first attempt.

Sri Lanka’s Tharindu Dasun Samaraweera, also going for his maiden jump, cramps up midway through the run-up. Not the start he would have hoped for.

Welsh para athlete Ellie Bowen is now the new leader courtesy her third throw of 6.48m, a new Personal Best for her.

Cook Islands’ Samasoni Hewitt had three failed attempts at 1.95m while Anguilla’s Johniff Gumbs, who twice failed to clear the same height, has pulled out of the competition.

Canada’s Claire Norek, the third name on the start list, takes the lead with a throw of 6.29m in her sixth and final attempt.

A commendable effort from India’s Swatik Patil as he finishes fifth in the men’s 100m breaststroke SB9 final with a timing of 1:15.82s.

Australia’s Beau Matthews (1:09.41s) takes the gold, New Zealand’s Joshua Willmer (1:11.44s) clinches the silver medal while the bronze goes to Australia’s Timothy Hodge (1:12.74s).

The bar has been raised to 1.95m but the Indian trio of Sarvesh Kushare, Tejaswin Shankar and Aadarsh Ram is yet to jump.

The second competitor - England’s Ozioma Nlewedum - is done with her six attempts and she manages a best effort of 5.31m, nine centimetres shorter than Hooker.

The Commonwealth Games 2026 official results website caused confusion on Monday after listing India’s Tejaswin Shankar as DNS for the men’s high jump final, even as the live telecast showed him at Scotstoun Stadium and ready to compete.

The official startlist still shows a DNS (Did not start) but Tejaswin Shankar is amongst the athletes being introduced to the crowd before the start of the men’s high jump final.

Every competitor will take all her six attempts one after the other.

Australia’s Ainsley Hooker starts the competition and her best effort is 5.40m, which came from her opening throw.

Tejaswin Shankar, the bronze medallist from the previous edition, will not compete in the men’s high jump final.

The update startlist shows a DNS (Did Not Start) against his name.

11:35 PM - Sharmila Dhankar and Shilpa K. Shyla, women’s shot put F57 final

11:40 PM - Sarvesh Kushare, Aadarsh Ram, men’s high jump final (medal event)

12 midnight - India vs Nigeria, women’s 3x3 wheelchair basketball Pool B match

12:02 AM - Swatik Patil - Men’s 100m Breaststroke SB9 Final (medal event)

12:45 AM - Ajaya Babu, men’s 79kg weightlifting final (medal event)

1:00 AM - Sumit Kundu vs Jon McConnell (Northern Ireland), men’s 70kg Boxing, Round of 16

1:07 AM - Aryan Nehra, men’s 800m freestyle swimming fastest heat/final (medal event)

1:44 AM - Sajan Prakash, men’s 200m butterfly swimming final (medal event)

1:57 AM - Rakeshbhai Bhatt and Shreyansh Trivedi, men’s 100m T38 final (para athletics, medal event)

2:15 AM - Tejas Shirse, men’s 110m hurdles final (medal event)

Sakshi lands a straight punch to Lethabo’s face with a minute remaining. However, she has a point deducted for dangerous use of her head. Lethabo had also received a warning and a point deduction earlier in the round. The referee brings both boxers to the centre of the ring before Sakshi is declared the winner by unanimous decision and advances to the quarterfinals.

Sakshi lands a sharp right-left combination, follows it with a jab, and then connects with a double jab to finish the round strongly. Lethabo shows improvement, but Sakshi once again sweeps all five judges’ scorecards and takes a commanding lead after the opening two rounds.

Sakshi lands several clean straight punches and takes the opening round on all five judges’ scorecards. The Indian is in a commanding position heading into Round 2.

Sakshi with some neat footwork, and we have just about 30 seconds left before the end of Round 1.

Three-time age-group world champion Sakshi Chaudhary will take on Botswana’s Lethabo Modukanele in the women’s 51kg round of 16 shortly. Modukanele is the Birmingham 2022 bronze medallist and the first woman boxer from Botswana to win a Commonwealth Games medal.

India’s Bindyarani Devi Sorokhaibam grabbed a bronze medal in the women’s 58kg weightlifting event at the Commonwealth Games 2026 in Glasgow on Monday.

Rafiatu Lawal completes a perfect series, clearing 117kg, 122kg and 126kg in the clean and jerk. Her final lift takes her total to 229kg, sealing the gold medal by a commanding 14kg and completing a sweep of Games records in the snatch, clean and jerk and total. She celebrates with Cristiano Ronaldo’s trademark ‘Siuuu’ celebration. The Birmingham 2022 champion is on top of the Commonwealth Games podium once again.

Canada’s Ann Sophie wins the silver medal after successfully lifting 121kg, a six-kilogram increase from her second attempt of 115kg.

Bindyarani Devi fails in her third attempt at 116kg. The silver medallist from the previous Commonwealth Games could not complete the lift. She is currently in the silver-medal position but will be pushed down to bronze if Rafiatu Lawal successfully lifts 117kg.

It is the end of the night for England’s Eliza Pratt. Her third attempt at 113kg is unsuccessful, and she has to settle for a bronze medal, mostly. She totals 196.

Bindyarani Devi comes back for her second lift and goes for 112kg, which she does cleanly. There are three green lights. She moves into the silver medal position. She has one more lift left.

Bindyarani Devi makes it look easy. She lifted 115kg earlier and now lifts 110kg on her first attempt. There’s a yellow flag..

And the jury has revoked her lift. It is ‘no lift’.

England’s Eliza Pratt successfully lifts 109kg, increasing her lead to a total of 196 points. She is attempting to go for 111kg in her final clean and jerk lift.

England’s Eliza Pratt lifts 106kg on her first attempt and is aiming for 108kg on her second attempt. She is currently leading the leaderboard.

Ashley Kolomoisky successfully lifts 104kg on her second attempt and is going for 106kg on her third lift. She currently leads with a total of 188 points.

South Africa’s Anneke Burger successfully lifts 101kg after summoning all her strength to complete the attempt. She will go for 103kg in her final attempt.She goes for 103, and there are two green lights, and the jury takes a look at it -- and it is a ‘no lift’. She had her elbows locked, and it shouldn’t be like that.

Kolomoisky lifts 100 kg successfully in her first clean and jerk attempt and goes straight to the top of the leaderboard.

Ioannou had 11 seconds remaining when she began her attempt. By the time she had the barbell over her shoulders, only one second remained. However, she could not hold her ground, and the attempt was unsuccessful. She finishes with a total of 160kg.

It is unfortunate. Anoni Faumui breaks down in a very similar way to her previous lift. She is unsuccessful in her second attempt once again at 95kg. She has another chance left.

Twenty-year-old Anoni Faumui attempted 95kg in her first clean and jerk attempt but was unsuccessful. She got the barbell up to her chest but could not complete the lift.

Cyprus’ Dimitra Ioannou successfully lifts 85kg in her first clean and jerk attempt and is going for 90kg next.Her second attempt: Three green lights in her favour and a successful lift.

Five kilos shy of her lifetime best, she had two attempts to match it. The second lift of 80 was successful, but the jury called it off, and she tried again, but it didn’t work out. She has a total of 140, with a best clean and jerk of 75kg.

Margarett Harris, who lifted 75kg in her first clean and jerk attempt, successfully lifts 80kg to match her lifetime best. She finishes with a total of 145kg.Wait, there’s drama: the jury has come back to judge her second lift as ‘no lift’.

Rafiatu Lawal holds a healthy advantage over the rest of the leaderboard after successful lifts of 95kg, 100kg and 103kg. Bindyarani Devi also completed all three attempts, with a best lift of 87kg. She will next attempt 113kg in the clean and jerk.

Unbelievable performance from the reigning champion. After beginning with 95kg, she followed it up with a successful lift of 100kg.

And now, she finishes the snatch with a Commonwealth Record of 103kg!

Canada’s Ann Sophie Taschereau is second with 94kg while India’s Bindyarani Devi is third with 87kg.

We’ll be back with the clean & jerk segment in a few minutes.

After two failed attempts at 94kg, the Canadian finally gets a clean lift on the third and final try. From almost exiting the competition, she is now at the top.

However, there is one more weightlifter to go - Nigeria’s Rafiatu Folashade Lawal. And she goes to the top of the chart with her very first lift of 95kg, breaking the Games Record set moments ago by Taschereau!

Smooth third attempt for India’s Bindyarani Devi, this time at 87kg, matching Pratt’s best snatch lift.

Australia’s Ashley Kolomoisky (84kg) and England’s Eliza Pratt (84kg) have overtaken Bindyarani but the Indian has two more snatch attempts to go. The Australian is done with all her three attempts while Pratt has one remaining.

The Indian is back in front with her lift of 85kg in her second attempt but not for long as Pratt shows great determination in her third attempt, registering a successful lift at 87kg.

India’s Bindyarani Devi, who had initially registered 85kg as her opening attempt in snatch, begins at 83kg and it is a clean lift.

Harris goes for 70kg while Ioannou tries to lift 75kg. However, it’s a no lift for both the weightlifters. But they have something on the board and so, will get a chance in the clean & jerk.

The next few weightlifters have also got something on the board in the snatch.

Anoni Faumui of Samoa currently leads with a successful lift of 82kg in her third and final attempt. However, a few competitors are yet to even start.

Nauru’s Margarett Bless Harris fails in her opening snatch attempt set at 60kg.

No issues for Dimitra Ioannou of Cyprus who completes the 65kg snatch.

Margarett increases the weight to 65kg from her opening attempt and this time, she completes the lift!

Another successful lift for Cyprian Ioannou, this time at 70kg.

​CWG 2026, Medals Tally, Live: Gyaneshwari Yadav clinches silver; India tally increases to fiveCWG 2026 Medals Tally Live: Follow India’s performances at the 2026 Commonwealth Games with the real-time medal tracker.​

CWG 2026 Medals Tally Live: Follow India’s performances at the 2026 Commonwealth Games with the real-time medal tracker.

Bindyarani Devi is set to feature in the women’s 58kg weightlifting final. She is starting with 85kg in the snatch section.

Gyaneshwari clears her opening clean-and-jerk mark of 103kg. Didih hardly breaks a sweat while going for 105kg as well. The combined lift is already a Commonwealth and Games record. This is now a two-way battle for gold, with the Nigerian holding a big advantage.

107 done for Gyaneshwari. This is now a GR in the clean and jerk. But she is still three kilos behind Didih’s mark. Make that eight, cause Didih clears 110. The record has moved against her name now. And it is a CR as well. The gold is all but hers.

Gyaneshwari lifts the revised 111kg off her last attempt. Ufff, what a performance this has been from the Indian!

But the Nigerian betters it at 113 to snatch the CR and GR again. A crazy few minutes these have been.

Didih wins gold with a combined lift worth 206kg, India gets silver with 199kg, and Groulx wins bronze with 178. There’s daylight between each of those tallies!

Taljaard’s opening 97kg effort has been challenged. It has been turned down after checking for a clean one-move lift. The 2017 African champion’s second attempt, however, is successful. That will temporarily push her into the silver medal position.

Wini pulls the bar way too close to her face. An unsuccessful effort at a 98kg lift. But she course-corrects in the final attempt; 98kg is hers to keep.

Groulx fails to bag a final 99kg. However, she remains well-placed to win the bronze medal in Glasgow after Taljaard gets three reds on a 101kg attempt.

Gulam loses her balance at 95kg. Another attempt to go. 92kg is what she will have to settle for, as the jerk proves to be too much for her on the last attempt. She will finish outside the medals.

Lagana, 18, looking to match her European best, tries 96 but fails. A successful lift would have temporarily seen her in a medal position.

Chua bows out with 94 as well, with 96 proving to be too much of an ask of her.

Was there a knee touch there? Lagana’s second attempt at 93kg gets the benefit of the doubt. The Jury didn’t object; perhaps it is the camera angle which deceives me.

Rebeka Groulx on the clock for her first attempt at 95kg. Gets all the lights on that one, but looked touch and go at one point.

Protistha Samanta is done with her vaults final at the Arena. With an average score of 12.883 and a bonus of 0.2, she is seemingly out of the medals.

We are back in time to catch Gyaneshwari equal Onome Omolola Didih’s Games record at 85kg.

Didih has two more attempts left, while Gyaneshwari has one. 88 is set on the bar. The Indian does it without breaking a sweat. While that is the new GR, the weight has now been revised to 90 for the Nigerian’s second attempt. And she has done it with another effort to go!

She clears 93kg as well. This is a new Commonwealth Record. Gyaneshwari has a deficit of five kilos heading into clean and jerk. Nine minutes to go for the second half.

Having established a comprehensive lead in the first rounds, Ankush looks to dominate the final three minutes of the contest against Zalaan Jan of Antigua and Barbuda. Uff, that would have hurt – a series of punches to Zalaan’s face. His coaches ask him to maintain distance from the sidelines. The referee asks Ankush to refrain from holding. Jan gets a bit of success while pinning Ankush to the ropes. Ankush runs down the clock on this extremely one-sided affair. He will be sailing into the quarterfinals with a unanimous 5-0 scoreline.

Taljaard almost makes a mess of her second lift. It looked like she would drop the barbell again, but minor adjustments while on her haunches contribute to the rescue act.

Kean ends her snatch with a best attempt of 73kg.

Looked like Wini had cleared 77kg, but three reds lit up. There is an ongoing team challenge. The decision remains the same, though. A bend in the elbow causes her undoing.

Chua matches her lifetime best of 74kg. Johanni Taljaard is here after taking some time off the sport. The South African drops 75kg. Gulam gets the greens on 75 as well. Brilliantly done!

The final attempt for Lagana. She may have struggled at 72kg but has no issues seeing off the 73kg mark. She lives.

Athens 2004 sixth-placed Toua is eliminated while trying to get 73kg on the board in snatch. It seems like only a few years ago when she was lifting 84kg.

Chua fails to get a successful 74kg lift off her second attempt. Experienced lifter Jenly Tegu Wini has her campaign up and running with 74kg.

Lagana fails to match her lifetime best mark (72kg) from the European Championships this year. Brenna Mae Kean, fifth-placed at CWG 2022 and Commonwealth Championships bronze medallist, loses her shape while attempting a 73kg lift. Papua New Guinea’s Loa Dika Toua fails to get a successful 73kg lift. Noorin Gulam, the reigning British champion, off to a good start with a 73kg lift. Kean gets 73 on the board. Smiles and cheekily holds her tongue out in celebration.

Malta’s Kim Camilleri Lagana has a successful lift of 70kg in snatch. 27-year-old Jiin Linn Chua lifts 71 next.

Gyaneshwari Yadav, all of 23 and the Asian Championship silver medallist, will shoulder India’s hopes in women’s 53kg weightlifting. Her best figures are 83kg in snatch and 103kg in clean and jerk, which is right at the top of the pile. So, we have a bit of time before catching a first glimpse of her.

In the men’s 100 metre backstroke SB9 event, Swatik Patil also qualified for the final after finishing fourth in Heat 2 with a time of 1:15.85 minutes.

The final of the SB9 event is scheduled to take place at 12:02 AM on Tuesday, July 28.

READ MORE ON THE SAME BY CLICKING ON THE PICTURE BELOW:

Sajan Prakash qualifies for the men's 200 metre butterfly final at CWG 2026, finishing second in Heat 2.

Vijender Singh’s nephew, Sachin, takes to the ring. He will go up against 24-year-old William Hewitt of England.

Sachin, in the red corner, starts off cautiously as Hewitt unleashes a quick series of counterattacking punches. Both trade blows in equal measure, and it may be difficult to separate the pugilists at the end of the first round. Four of the five judges vote in favour of Sachin going into the next.

Sachin’s backhand has been blocked effectively by the English boxer. The Indian leans in next, but an alert Hewitt evades the punch. Sachin has two of his punches land as the Indian crowd gets behind him. The same four judges rule in favour of the Indian again. He has a point deducted after being given a warning.

Sachin avoids a hit by moving to his right. Hewitt blocks one next. The referee briefly stops the contest to warn Hewitt about his head position. The left backhand comes to Sachin’s aid again.

As the bell goes off, it seems like Sachin’s done enough. He feels the same as he raises his arms up high.

And it is official... the Indian is moving to the next round. He will meet Treasure Moremi of Botswana.

While the writing was already on the wall, Gurindervir’s 10.39 will not be good enough to carry him into the top 17 who will make the 100m semifinal.

Lokesh has a great opening jump. Just 3.9cm on the floorboard at kickoff, and a 7.77m jump will get his qualification started.

He has jumped to the top of the Group B leaderboard.

While there is some time until the official confirmation comes, this leap is good enough for Lokesh to make the final day after tomorrow.

Sreeshankar’s automatic qualification off the very first jump may have put undue pressure on the Bengaluru-born Lokesh. He will be the last in the Group B field to attempt an 8.00m jump.

The first three finishers are set to qualify for the final.

England’s Sam Bennett is off to a great start: doesn’t really attack the first hurdle but he will have the Jamaican Jerome Campbell breathing down his neck.

Tejas is way behind and upsets the seventh hurdle, but the Indian won’t mind, for he finishes third with 13.76. That will be good enough to take him to the final later tonight.

Bennett finishes the race in 13.20s, Campbell second with 13.33. A +2.1m/s wind has robbed Bennett of a potential record.

The introductions begin for men’s 110m hurdles Round 1 - Heat 1. Tejas Shirse, on lane 7, chooses not to look at the camera at all. Focus seems to be the mantra of the evening.

A dream swim from Sajan Prakash in the men’s 200m butterfly heats.

The start isn’t as great. He is fourth after the first 50m, but an excellent recovery sees the Indian leave everyone behind after 100m in 56.31. However, home favourite Duncan Scott pushes ahead in the latter half, leaving a 0.30s gap between the top two.

1:58.59 on the clock makes Sajan an automatic qualifier. The eight fastest from the heats qualify for the final.

Time for Sreeshankar’s first jump. The qualification mark is set at 8.00m. All athletes crossing the said mark or at least the 12 best performers advance.

He takes some big strides in the buildup... that’s a brilliant kickoff, and he is way behind the orange line. That will count as a legal jump.

There’s the confirmation... 8.01m it is, and he has already made the final.

National record holder Gurindervir Singh has his eyes closed in a silent prayer during the introductions. He would be hoping to equal his 10.09, if not better the mark today!

Off we go... Rohan Watson and Gurindervir are off to a great start but the Jamaican comfortably pulls away in the last 30m.

A 10.13s finish for Watson and 10.39 for Gurindervir.

The 17 fastest athletes from the 11 Heats make the semifinal.

It’s drizzling ever so slightly at Scotstoun Stadium. The temperature is 15 degrees as the men’s 100m heats begin.

Seven athletes have been given a bye into the semifinals. Gurindervir Singh will be the first Indian in action in Heat 4.

As expected, Favour Ashe of Nigeria comfortably finishes ahead of the rest of the pack in Heat 1 in 10.10.

Abdul-Rasheed Saminu absolutely crushes his heats in the second round with a 10.01. That’s the fastest ever timing recorded in a Commonwealth Games opening round. Also, it is a season best for the Ghanaian.

Wales’ Jeremiah Azu, with the wind behind him, also completes his race in 10.10 in Heat 3. Sri Lanka’s Dineth Weeraratna registers 10.33, a personal best.

content.title: CWG 2026 Glasgow LIVE Updates, Day 5: Sharmila wins gold in women's shot put F57, Kushare bags silver in high jump
content.author: Unknown Author

markdown_content:
## Welcome

Welcome to Sportstar’s live coverage of Day 5 of the 23rd Commonwealth Games in Glasgow.

## Schedule highlights

- Multiple athletics events: men’s long jump qualification, 100m heats, 110m hurdles
- Para athletics: shot put F57 final
- Several weightlifting finals
- Swimming heats and finals
- Active boxing card

## Weightlifting

The women’s 58kg and men’s 79kg competitions provided drama. India’s Bindyarani Devi took bronze in the women’s 58kg after a strong snatch phase and an intense clean-and-jerk segment. Bindyarani recorded 85kg in the snatch section and matched other competitors with efforts in the clean-and-jerk, but a final 116kg attempt was unsuccessful. Rafiatu Lawal of Nigeria dominated her category, lifting a Games and Commonwealth record total to take gold. Canada’s Ann Sophie Taschereau claimed silver in several weight classes mentioned across the session.

Gyaneshwari Yadav produced a superb performance in the women’s 53kg weightlifting, matching and then chasing Games records in a thrilling duel with Nigeria’s Onome Omolola Didih. Gyaneshwari lifted impressive weights (clean and jerk attempts up to 111kg) and finished with a 199kg total to secure silver, while Didih took gold with 206kg. The competition featured multiple lead changes and several records being set and then bettered.

## Shot put F57

Sharmila Dhankar delivered a landmark moment for India, winning gold in the women’s shot put F57 with a best throw of 9.81m. Her victory ended India’s 20-year wait for a Para Athletics medal at the Commonwealth Games, making her the country’s first-ever CWG gold medallist in Para Athletics and the first Indian woman to win a Para Athletics medal at the Games. Shilpa K. Shyla moved into bronze position after a judge review in another event.

## High jump

The men’s high jump final featured strong Indian representation. Sarvesh Kushare produced a steady series of clearances and secured the silver medal after clearing heights including a crucial 2.25m on his final attempt. Jamaica’s Romaine Beckford and others battled up the leaderboard, with countback and failed attempts deciding final positions. Aadarsh Ram moved into the top standings early with a 2.10m clearance but finished outside the medals after later failures. Tejaswin Shankar, who had been listed inconsistently on the official startlist, was ruled DNS for the final and later cited a knee issue that prevented him from competing further.

## Athletics qualifying

Murali Sreeshankar automatically qualified for the long jump final with an opening legal jump of 8.01m. Lokesh Sathyanathan also secured a spot in the final from Group B with a decisive opening leap, and Tejas Shirse progressed from the 110m hurdles heats and later reached the final despite a concerning performance in the final where he finished eighth and appeared injured.

## Swimming and para-swimming

Sajan Prakash qualified for the men’s 200m butterfly final with a strong heat, and Swatik Patil advanced to the men’s 100m breaststroke SB9 final. Aryan Nehra finished seventh in the 800m freestyle fastest heat, while other Indian swimmers posted competitive times but missed podium spots.

## Boxing

Several Indian boxers advanced through round of 16 bouts. Sakshi Chaudhary won convincingly against Botswana’s Lethabo Modukanele by unanimous decision and progressed to the quarterfinals. Sachin (Vijender Singh’s nephew) claimed victory over England’s William Hewitt and moved into the next round. Sumit Kundu’s contest against Northern Ireland’s Jon McConnell ended in a split-decision defeat after a tightly scored bout.

## Other notes and incidents

- The Commonwealth Games official results website briefly listed Tejaswin Shankar as DNS, causing confusion when broadcast coverage showed him present.
- Tactical decisions in boxing included point deductions and warnings.
- Jury reviews in weightlifting overturned or upheld attempts during the session.
- Several athletes pulled out due to cramps or injury.
- India’s women’s wheelchair 3x3 basketball team finished their group stage with a loss to Nigeria, ending their campaign.

## Summary

Overall, Day 5 combined medal success for India in para athletics and weightlifting with several athletes securing finals in athletics and swimming. Medical updates on a few injured competitors and ongoing appeals or jury decisions will shape the coming days as India chases more medals in Glasgow.

Source: Live coverage and event reports from Scotstoun Stadium and weightlifting venues, Glasgow.
